findings.description: The reports bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so archived reports are stored under S3's default (SSE-S3 or, where unset, no managed key) rather than an explicitly enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 policy.
The ledger exports bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so exported financial ledger data is not encrypted under a managed key.
The model artifacts bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so model data and training artifacts are stored without an explicitly configured default encryption key.
The runbooks bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so operational runbooks are not encrypted under a managed key.

The audit trail bucket sets acl = "log-delivery-write" but has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block":"none and no public access block resource, leaving the bucket that stores the account's audit logs without a guard against public exposure.

The seed object is uploaded to the reports_archive bucket, which has no server_side_encryption_configuration and therefore no enforced default key; the object is stored without managed encryption and no explicit encryption attribute is set on the object.

force_destroy = true on the audit trail bucket allows the access logs and audit records for the account to be destroyed by a routine terraform apply, undermining the tamper-evidence of the logging pipeline.
